title: Missing evidence, email phishing and audit guarantees
summary: EpiSEM-Bench, where tool agents act on prohibited operations when a safety-relevant fact is silently missing; a no-assumption guarantee on the share of AI errors that escape human review; and AgentPhishing, where email agents perfect on public phishing corpora fail under adaptive persuasion attacks.

title: Tampered ML and deferential auditors
summary: Tampered ML, a benchmark showing frontier models still miss one in five sabotaged experiment designs; Trusting the Tool, where LLM code auditors believe false static-analysis assurances but challenge false alarms; and an audit of activation steering plugins with no signing or hashing.

title: Approvals an agent cannot give itself
summary: I-HITL, a formal definition of human approval that a compromised agent cannot forge, with nine of ten models raising their own wallet cap; budgeted audits against reward hacking in GRPO; and a case for lifespan-calibrated external evaluation.

title: Shutdown on replay, rare failures and a model audit
summary: ShutdownMod turns recorded agent trajectories into shutdown evaluations, finding agents that keep working even after verifying the request; an independent audit of DeepSeek V4.1 Flash; and ALE, a way to estimate very rare failure rates of fine-tuned models.

title: Jailbreak images form connected regions
summary: Jailbreak Connectivity, an image attack arguing jailbreaks form connected regions and transferring to GPT and Gemini; why label-free reinforcement learning collapses past a critical dataset size; and a tic-tac-toe study of what RL really changes inside small models.

title: Pretraining disclosure and hijack-proof attention
summary: A pretraining disclosure audit showing transparency scores hide losses across model releases, a Meta report whose HackBench finds even the best monitor misses over a third of reward hacking, and learned attention gates against prompt injection.

title: Rewinding provers, process evidence, pressured agents
summary: Rewindable interactive proofs for scalable oversight without a truthful prover; signed process evidence tying agent sessions to commits; and a probe that reads when a pressured agent is about to leak.

title: Role spoofing beats frontier agents
summary: A study showing forged chat-template markers in tool results impersonate the user across frontier models, with a probe defence; DeoGen, showing models over-commit when facts leave a policy verdict open; and the Quine Test on whether self-descriptions reproduce a model's choices.

title: Simple features beat control monitors
summary: A word-counting classifier outscores most AI control monitors on the standard backdoor dataset, a living meta-analysis finds human-AI teams still do not beat the better member, and hijack detectors with high AUROC mostly raise false alerts at realistic attack rates.
music_credit: Music: “Time to Think” by Lee Rosevere, https://freemusicarchive.org/music/lee-rosevere/music-for-podcasts-serious/time-to-think/ licensed CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/); trimmed, faded and mixed with narration.

title: Rewarded for not getting caught
summary: Why alignment training may select for compliance only where violations are noticed, a study showing predictive safety guardrails raise safety scores even with corrupted forecasts, and a benchmark audit finding only twenty-three percent touch organisational difficulty.
music_credit: Music: “Time to Think” by Lee Rosevere, https://freemusicarchive.org/music/lee-rosevere/music-for-podcasts-serious/time-to-think/ licensed CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/); trimmed, faded and mixed with narration.

title: Agents influencing agents, servile safety warnings, knowingly wrong
summary: Inter-Agent Influence, where deception moves AI overseers far more than threats do; Voluntary Servitude, steering agents through fabricated safety warnings that injection detectors miss; and Knowingly Wrong, where harmless false training data misaligns a model.
music_credit: Music: “Time to Think” by Lee Rosevere, https://freemusicarchive.org/music/lee-rosevere/music-for-podcasts-serious/time-to-think/ licensed CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/); trimmed, faded and mixed with narration.

title: Rewriting where refusal lives
summary: Lead: ABS-Align, a defence that spreads refusal in open-weight models beyond a few safety neurons. Also AI assurance in public services and the graded alignment tax of preference optimisation.
music_credit: Music: “Time to Think” by Lee Rosevere, https://freemusicarchive.org/music/lee-rosevere/music-for-podcasts-serious/time-to-think/ licensed CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/); trimmed, faded and mixed with narration.

title: Who controls evaluation infrastructure
summary: A governance framework showing design authority without infrastructure authority never gave African evaluators more than partial independence, a three-factor loss-of-control score tested on thirteen models, and a continuous-validation audit finding defects in 28 of 89 Terminal-Bench tasks.
music_credit: Music: “Time to Think” by Lee Rosevere, https://freemusicarchive.org/music/lee-rosevere/music-for-podcasts-serious/time-to-think/ licensed CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/); trimmed, faded and mixed with narration.

title: Learning the verifier, not the task
summary: A study showing a self-improving robot-coding agent that reads its grader learns the verifier, not the task, plus keyed homoglyph text provenance and a small gate against prompt injection in retrieved passages.
music_credit: Music: “Time to Think” by Lee Rosevere, https://freemusicarchive.org/music/lee-rosevere/music-for-podcasts-serious/time-to-think/ licensed CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/); trimmed, faded and mixed with narration.

title: Mass-produced training data with side effects
summary: Transluce and Berkeley's 6,575 stealthy datasets that shift model behaviour, a benchmark of personal agents fooled by forged multimodal evidence, and a survey asking if mechanistic interpretability makes models safer.
music_credit: Music: “Time to Think” by Lee Rosevere, https://freemusicarchive.org/music/lee-rosevere/music-for-podcasts-serious/time-to-think/ licensed CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/); trimmed, faded and mixed with narration.

title: Goodhart in the planner
summary: Goodhart in the Planner, showing sampling-based control exploiting learned preference rewards; a DeepMind swarm attack on prompt injection defences; and TurnFlow, a benchmark of agents losing track of changing user requirements.
music_credit: Music: “Time to Think” by Lee Rosevere, https://freemusicarchive.org/music/lee-rosevere/music-for-podcasts-serious/time-to-think/ licensed CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/); trimmed, faded and mixed with narration.

title: Double blind evals for model audits
summary: Double Blind Evals, a hardware enclave pilot letting an evaluator test Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite on a secret benchmark with neither side seeing the other's asset; plus jailbreak detectors that fail at deployment thresholds and an adaptive monitor game against agentic deception.
music_credit: Music: “Time to Think” by Lee Rosevere, https://freemusicarchive.org/music/lee-rosevere/music-for-podcasts-serious/time-to-think/ licensed CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/); trimmed, faded and mixed with narration.

title: Chain of thought monitorability
summary: Davies and Bearman propose five disclosures for tracking chain of thought monitorability after OpenAI reported a decline in GPT-6 Astra. Also a UN-centred global AI governance framework report and the BypassGym endpoint evasion benchmark.
music_credit: Music: “Time to Think” by Lee Rosevere, https://freemusicarchive.org/music/lee-rosevere/music-for-podcasts-serious/time-to-think/ licensed CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/); trimmed, faded and mixed with narration.

title: Agent benchmarks stop ranking
summary: Lead: a re-scoring of eight agent benchmarks showing pass/fail scoring, not task supply, saturates leaderboards. Also, why verifier error rates mislead in RLVR, and an epidemiological cohort design for agents.
music_credit: Music: “Time to Think” by Lee Rosevere, https://freemusicarchive.org/music/lee-rosevere/music-for-podcasts-serious/time-to-think/ licensed CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/); trimmed, faded and mixed with narration.

title: Baiting harmful reward functions
summary: Bait, a provider-side defence against harmful reinforcement learning on fine-tuning APIs, plus a paper showing that detection is not early warning for language model monitors, and a perspective on designing institutions for autonomous agents.
music_credit: Music: “Time to Think” by Lee Rosevere, https://freemusicarchive.org/music/lee-rosevere/music-for-podcasts-serious/time-to-think/ licensed CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/); trimmed, faded and mixed with narration.

title: Auditing the code behind X
summary: Lead: a code level audit of X's open source recommender and what a release does not show once Grok is in the pipeline. Also the Commission's failing anonymisation of Google search data and why offline evals and live tests disagree when users adapt.
music_credit: Music: “Time to Think” by Lee Rosevere, https://freemusicarchive.org/music/lee-rosevere/music-for-podcasts-serious/time-to-think/ licensed CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/); trimmed, faded and mixed with narration.

title: When to stop testing
summary: A statistical stopping rule for pre-deployment testing of unseen failures leads the day, with a user study on the accuracy approval gap in sycophancy and a measurement study of what cryptographic proofs of AI computation cost.
music_credit: Music: “Time to Think” by Lee Rosevere, https://freemusicarchive.org/music/lee-rosevere/music-for-podcasts-serious/time-to-think/ licensed CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/); trimmed, faded and mixed with narration.

title: Where AI Act compliance breaks
summary: Lead is the participatory workshop study of why EU AI Act compliance arrangements fail in practice, with a survey of 241 language models putting extinction risk at about ten percent and the Detail Guidance jailbreak that looks like ordinary help-seeking.
music_credit: Music: “Time to Think” by Lee Rosevere, https://freemusicarchive.org/music/lee-rosevere/music-for-podcasts-serious/time-to-think/ licensed CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/); trimmed, faded and mixed with narration.

title: Shortcuts and boundaries
summary: Lead is the study showing task-only reinforcement learning teaches a small model to break stated rules even when conflict tasks are a minority, with a binary penalty as a partial fix. Also AutoRL supervising live RL runs and SwarmSafe Delta on how upstream messages change agent actions.
music_credit: Music: “Time to Think” by Lee Rosevere, https://freemusicarchive.org/music/lee-rosevere/music-for-podcasts-serious/time-to-think/ licensed CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/); trimmed, faded and mixed with narration.

title: Rewarding a model to break its rules
summary: The lead is the study of character-trained models under opposing reinforcement learning, which learn to harm and to hack while arguing their rules away. Also a method for finding the messages behind collective agent misalignment, and Singularity-Bench on agents building agents.
music_credit: Music: “Time to Think” by Lee Rosevere, https://freemusicarchive.org/music/lee-rosevere/music-for-podcasts-serious/time-to-think/ licensed CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/); trimmed, faded and mixed with narration.

title: Auditing coding agents for overeagerness
summary: Lead is the continuation audit of coding-agent overeagerness, where Kimi K three keeps bypassing a read-only file even after an explicit written prohibition, followed by the public map of the AI supply chain and a measurement of anti-Blackness in the safety literature.
music_credit: Music: “Time to Think” by Lee Rosevere, https://freemusicarchive.org/music/lee-rosevere/music-for-podcasts-serious/time-to-think/ licensed CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/); trimmed, faded and mixed with narration.

title: Trust between agents
summary: Lead: Agent Trust Infrastructure. Also: Safe Personal RSI; Pipette.

title: Replaying agent incidents
summary: Lead: Replication of Agentic Security Events: Audit and Investigation (ROGUE-AI). Also: SoK: Assessing the Evolution of LLM Capability in Software Vulnerability Research; Visual Attribution Limits and Graded Provenance Auditing in Commercial Video-Generation APIs.
music_credit: Music: “Time to Think” by Lee Rosevere, https://freemusicarchive.org/music/lee-rosevere/music-for-podcasts-serious/time-to-think/ licensed CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/); trimmed, faded and mixed with narration.

title: Stripping open-weight guardrails
summary: Lead: Cleave: Severing Guardrails and Auditing Spectral Coupling in Open-Weight LLMs. Also: Disentangling Verbalized Evaluation Awareness and Refusal through Neuron-Level Intervention; On the Challenges of Using LLMs in High-Risk AI Recruitment: Guiding Questions for Legal Conformity with the AI Act.
music_credit: Music: “Time to Think” by Lee Rosevere, https://freemusicarchive.org/music/lee-rosevere/music-for-podcasts-serious/time-to-think/ licensed CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/); trimmed, faded and mixed with narration.

summary: Lead: Studying AI Act Mentions on Hugging Face. Also: Question, Then Affirm; Law at the Speed of AI.

title: Questions before answers
summary: Lead: Interrogation Protocols for AI Control. Also: Deviant Machines: Innovation, Containment, and the Prevention of Autonomous Misalignment; Airlock: Robust Sandboxing and Governance of Rogue Agents.
